#!/bin/bash
# usage: check.sh <checkout> <label>
# Gmail-mode profile upgrade check: a profile written by main 83e9c3b (through the real GmailCore
# and store) must read back identically under <checkout>'s code, reopen idempotently, and end
# with the same schema as a profile created fresh by that code.
C="$1"; L="$2"; G="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"; W="$G/$L"; rm -rf "$W"; mkdir -p "$W/proj"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target
FAIL=0; ok(){ echo "  ok   $*"; }; bad(){ echo "  FAIL $*"; FAIL=1; }
cp -r "$G/template/." "$W/proj/"; sed -i "s#__MAILCORE__#$C/crates/mail-core#" "$W/proj/Cargo.toml"; cp "$C/Cargo.lock" "$W/proj/Cargo.lock"
echo "== gmail upgrade check $L at $(git -C "$C" rev-parse --short HEAD)"
( cd /home/exedev/email-os && mise exec -- cargo build --offline --manifest-path "$W/proj/Cargo.toml" >"$W/build.log" 2>&1 ) || { echo "  HARNESS BUILD FAILED (API change?)"; grep -E '^error' -A6 "$W/build.log" | head -30; exit 2; }
cp "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/gmail-upgrade-check" "$W/bin"
schema(){ sqlite3 "$1/gmail.db" "select type||' '||name||' '||coalesce(sql,'') from sqlite_master where name not like 'sqlite_%' order by name" | tr -s ' \n\t' ' '; }
ver(){ sqlite3 "$1/gmail.db" "select value from meta where key='schema_version'"; }
cp -a "$G/seed" "$W/upgraded"
echo "  seed profile schema_version: $(ver "$G/seed")"
"$W/bin" dump "$W/upgraded" >"$W/dump-1.json" 2>"$W/dump-1.err" || bad "dump under new code failed: $(tail -2 "$W/dump-1.err")"
diff -q "$G/dump-base-1.json" "$W/dump-1.json" >/dev/null && ok "profile from main reads back identically under new code" || { bad "read-back differs from main"; diff "$G/dump-base-1.json" "$W/dump-1.json" | head -30; }
"$W/bin" dump "$W/upgraded" >"$W/dump-2.json" 2>/dev/null; diff -q "$W/dump-1.json" "$W/dump-2.json" >/dev/null && ok "reopen is idempotent" || bad "second open changed what is read"
echo "  upgraded schema_version: $(ver "$W/upgraded")"
mkdir -p "$W/fresh"; "$W/bin" seed "$W/fresh" >"$W/seed-fresh.log" 2>&1 || bad "seeding a fresh profile under new code failed: $(tail -3 "$W/seed-fresh.log")"
echo "  fresh schema_version:    $(ver "$W/fresh")"
[ "$(ver "$W/upgraded")" = "$(ver "$W/fresh")" ] && ok "upgraded and fresh profiles record the same version" || bad "version differs between upgraded and fresh"
schema "$W/upgraded" | tr ' ' '\n' | sort >"$W/schema-upgraded.txt"; schema "$W/fresh" | tr ' ' '\n' | sort >"$W/schema-fresh.txt"
diff -q "$W/schema-upgraded.txt" "$W/schema-fresh.txt" >/dev/null && ok "upgraded schema equals fresh schema (token-wise)" || { bad "schema differs between upgraded and fresh"; diff "$W/schema-upgraded.txt" "$W/schema-fresh.txt" | head -20; }
"$W/bin" dump "$W/fresh" >"$W/dump-fresh.json" 2>/dev/null; diff -q "$G/dump-base-1.json" "$W/dump-fresh.json" >/dev/null && ok "a fresh profile seeded by new code reads the same as main's" || { echo "  note fresh-seeded dump differs from main's (ids/timestamps are expected to differ):"; diff "$G/dump-base-1.json" "$W/dump-fresh.json" | grep -c '^[<>]'; }
rm -f "$W/bin"
echo "== result: $([ $FAIL = 0 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL)"; exit $FAIL
EOF
chmod +x $S/gmail-upgrade/check.sh; $S/gmail-upgrade/check.sh $S/base-83e9c3b selftest 2>&1 | tail -14

**What Phase 3 produced in its 23 minutes**

A Gmail-mode upgrade check is now part of my merge gate. It seeds a profile through the real Gmail core using main's code (archive, mark read, a bulk archive, a saved split, a reminder, one queued action), then confirms the new code reads it back identically, reopens it without changes, and ends with the same schema as a fresh profile. That covers migration and store changes, which the fixture-mode app smoke does not exercise.

**Decision for you: how to continue without Codex**

## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)

1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.

## Risks and decision gates

A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.

The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.

You are one implementation thread in a coordinated maintenance programme for Email OS, following a code review. A coordinating thread (not you) sequences tickets, reviews and merges PRs, and runs end-to-end validation. This is implementation, not another review.

HOW TO WORK
- The user chose Claude Sonnet 5.5 for these threads. Where work splits cleanly into non-overlapping files, use your native subagents (Agent tool) on the same model, with full scoped briefs and the checkout path; you review and integrate. No other models. Do tightly coupled work yourself.
- Read the repository instructions, docs/current-architecture.md, docs/current-status.md and docs/development.md first.
- You are in an isolated worktree from origin/main at 5aa7dea. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os or its local .codex/hooks.json change.
- Commit and push at every checkpoint, and confirm each push landed (compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with `git ls-remote origin <branch>`; do not hide push output). Open each PR as a draft as soon as its first commit exists, and mark it ready when validated. The git remote is a proxy URL, so `gh` needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`.

MACHINE LIMITS
- 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, little free disk, shared with the coordinator's Rust gates and at most one other thread. Run one heavy command at a time, including across subagents.
- This ticket is frontend-only. Do not run cargo locally; CI on the PR covers the Rust suites. Use `mise run install:ui` once, then `mise run test:ui`, `mise run typecheck`, `mise run build:web` and the frontend lint task. If you ever need cargo, export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target first and never hardcode a target dir.
- Rendered browser suite (run once, on the final head only): `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome mise run test:rendered`. Baseline on main is 33 of 34: the large-text Inbox row overflow test fails because of a known product regression. Leave that test and that bug alone.

TICKET 19: split `useMailbox`
Facts on main: `src/composables/useMailbox.ts` is 2,072 lines; `useMailbox(client: MailClient): Mailbox` starts at about line 275 and the `Mailbox` interface at about line 137. The user's recent UI work already extracted `useReminders.ts` (391 lines), `useDrawerRows.ts` and `useDraftPreviews.ts`; follow the conventions those use. 22 source and test files import from `useMailbox`.

Extract, in this order, each into its own composable (or plain module where no reactivity is needed) under `src/composables/`:
1. selection (selected set, range/anchor behaviour, the `SELECTION_MAX` cap, pruning when rows leave);
2. group operations and recovery (group archive/read acceptance, group notices, undo of groups, recovery of interrupted or partially failed groups);
3. detail cache and prefetch (the bounded detail cache, TTL, prefetch, reader loading delay);
4. account lifecycle (connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions, cancel-upgrade, account state).
One PR per extraction, four PRs, each stacked on the previous: PR 1 targets main, PR 2 targets PR 1's branch, and so on. The coordinator merges in order and retargets. Branch names: maintenance/p5a-mailbox-selection (this worktree's branch), then maintenance/p5a-mailbox-groups, maintenance/p5a-mailbox-detail-cache, maintenance/p5a-mailbox-account.

Requirements
- Behaviour-preserving. `useMailbox(client)` and the `Mailbox` interface keep their exact public shape, and every name currently exported from `src/composables/useMailbox.ts` stays importable from that path (re-export where a definition moves), so no consumer has to change.
- HARD BOUNDARY: do not modify `src/App.vue`, `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts`, `src/lib/action-palette.ts`, `src/components/**`, `src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue` or `src/assets/style.css`. The user has an open UI PR (#34) in active work on those files, and any edit there creates conflicts for them. If an extraction cannot be done without touching one of them, stop and report.
- Keep session invalidation explicit. Today one composable shares the fences that drop stale responses after an account change, disconnect, reconnect or generation change. Each extracted piece must receive that session/generation dependency explicitly through its arguments (no module-level mutable state, no hidden coupling through closures over the parent), and for each piece name the existing test that proves a stale response is dropped after invalidation, or add one if none exists.
- No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement. Report frontend test counts before and after each PR (baseline on main: 1,454 tests in 84 files; confirm it yourself first). Add focused unit tests for an extracted composable where it is now testable in isolation and the existing component tests only cover it indirectly; do not duplicate coverage for its own sake. Use the shared helpers in `tests/helpers.ts` and `tests/support/`, fake timers, and the feature folders under `tests/`.
- Each PR should be reviewable as mostly moves: keep function bodies unchanged where possible, and list every non-move edit in the PR description (signature changes, new parameters, re-exports).
- Update docs/current-architecture.md in the PR that changes a boundary.
- Synthetic fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- If the ticket is wrong about the code, or you find a real bug or a product decision outside scope, stop and report with evidence instead of deciding it yourself.

DONE WHEN
- `useMailbox.ts` is mostly wiring for these four areas; report its line count and each new module's line count.
- On each PR head: `mise run test:ui`, typecheck, lint and `build:web` pass. On the final head, the rendered suite is 33 of 34 with only the known failure.

FINAL REPORT (your last message)
A table of PRs (number, URL, base, head SHA, CI state), test counts before and after, line counts, the list of non-move edits, the invalidation test named for each piece, anything you found that needs a decision, and anything you did not run.

The picture changed while I was paused: the P3a thread was continued on Sonnet 5.5 on 12 November and finished tickets 9, 10 and 12 as three stacked PRs (#46, #48, #49), none merged yet.

What I've done so far this turn:

- **Gate running on the top of the P3a stack** (`3e2ecfc`, all three tickets): core tests and the contract check have passed; lint, frontend, native, rendered, the native smoke and the Gmail upgrade check are still to come.
- **Reviewed all three diffs.**
  - #46 (migrations): the ordered steps reproduce the old probes, and crash recovery now runs as its own startup step after migration.
  - #48 (store split): a pure move — 7,946 of about 8,060 lines are identical, and the rest is visibility modifiers and module wiring.
  - #49 (error logging): a log line is built only from the source file and line, a static tag and numeric SQLite codes; error text is never read.
- **Launched [Email OS P5a: split useMailbox (T19)](t3-thread://v2/a54b6c0e-579e-4ecd-b328-bf6fee0ad1e4/mcp:launch:ac446ed3c33ae8f448ec486f9439559322e8df7afe78d2656ec3b4875166841c)** on Sonnet 5.5. PR #34 doesn't touch `useMailbox.ts`, so this ticket isn't blocked by it; the brief forbids edits to the files #34 does touch.
- **Deleted the scheduled 14 November resume**, since it would have restarted the Sol threads.

One consequence of #46 you should know before I merge it: once a build containing it opens your Gmail profile, the version marker advances, and older builds (including #34's branch until it is rebased on main) will refuse to open that profile. The data is untouched; only the marker changes.

Next, in order:

1. Merge #46, #48 and #49 once the gate is green.
2. Launch the provider trait rename (rest of ticket 11) from the new main.
3. Start Phase 4 with the shared contract scenarios (ticket 17), then the staged fixture unification (ticket 14), then the shell split (ticket 16).
4. Tickets 18 and 20 still wait on #34.

For Phase 4 I'm taking "run the remaining threads" as approval of my recommendation on ADR #45: unify onto the Gmail core, fixture mode gains read and star, fixture reminders follow the Gmail local rules, and fixture profiles get a one-time reset with a disclosure and a backup (drafts kept). The first two stages don't change fixture behaviour, so you can redirect before anything visible lands.

input.message:
You are one implementation thread in a coordinated maintenance programme for Email OS, following a code review. A coordinating thread (not you) sequences tickets, reviews and merges PRs, and runs end-to-end validation. This is implementation, not another review.

HOW TO WORK
- The user chose Claude Sonnet 5.5 for these threads. Where work splits cleanly into non-overlapping files, use your native subagents (Agent tool) on the same model, with full scoped briefs and the checkout path; you review and integrate. No other models. Do tightly coupled work yourself.
- Read the repository instructions, docs/current-architecture.md, docs/current-status.md and docs/development.md first.
- You are in an isolated worktree from origin/main at ede9d0b. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os or its local .codex/hooks.json change.
- Commit and push at every checkpoint, and confirm each push landed (compare `git rev-parse HEAD` with `git ls-remote origin <branch>`; do not hide push output). Open each PR as a draft as soon as its first commit exists, and mark it ready when validated. The git remote is a proxy URL, so `gh` needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`. CI runs only on PRs whose base is main.

MACHINE LIMITS
- 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 6 GB free disk, shared with one sibling thread (frontend-only: it is splitting `src/composables/useMailbox.ts`; stay out of `src/composables/`) and the coordinator's gates.
- Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target for every cargo/mise command (shared build cache; never hardcode a target dir). One heavy command at a time, including across subagents. Run `mise run install:ui` once before `mise run check:all`.
- Shared Rust test support exists: `mail_core::testing` behind the `test-support` feature (scripted fake provider, `until`, TempDir profiles, worker gates, fake clock). Use it; no new ad-hoc fakes, temp directories or sleeps. Frontend tests use `tests/helpers.ts`, `tests/support/` and fake timers.
- Baselines on main ede9d0b: mail-core 327 tests, email-os 14, frontend 1,454 in 84 files. No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement; report counts before and after.
- Synthetic fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials or Google network. Nothing mail-related (subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, ids in URLs) may be logged.
- HARD BOUNDARY: do not modify `src/App.vue`, `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts`, `src/lib/action-palette.ts`, `src/components/**`, `src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue` or `src/assets/style.css`; the user has an open UI PR (#34) in active work on them.
- If a ticket is wrong about the code, or you find a real bug or a decision outside scope, stop and report with evidence.

TWO TICKETS, TWO INDEPENDENT PRs (not stacked), IN THIS ORDER

TICKET 11, second half: fix the provider trait's name (PR A, small; do it first so it can merge while you work on PR B)
Facts on main: `pub trait GmailReadProvider: Send + Sync` in `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs` (about line 125) is not read-only. It carries auth and session (`is_configured`, `has_credentials`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `profile`), reads (`list_inbox`, `search_threads`, `get_thread`, `history`, the account-bound destination reads, `fetch_attachment`) and writes (`mutation_access`, `enable_mutations`, `apply_archive`, `apply_star`, `apply_read`). About 35 references across `gmail/operations.rs`, `gmail/provider.rs`, `gmail/provider/api.rs`, `gmail/sync.rs`, `gmail/types.rs`, `testing.rs`, `testing/operations_fake.rs`, two integration tests, `src-tauri/src/main.rs` and docs.
Do: rename it to `GmailProvider` everywhere in code and in docs that describe the current code (leave documents that are explicitly historical records as they are, following each document's own status header). Do not split the trait: the next phase adds a second, synthetic implementation of the whole surface, and no consumer today needs only a part. If you find a consumer that genuinely wants a narrower trait, report it rather than splitting. No behaviour change; the public Rust surface changes only by this name. Branch: maintenance/p3b-provider-trait-rename (this worktree's branch). Validate with `mise run check:all`.

TICKET 17: shared contract scenarios for the browser fake (PR B)
Background: the frontend runs against two implementations of one IPC contract: the Rust core behind Tauri, and `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` (1,946 lines) for browser development and most UI tests. Nothing forces them to agree, and the operation ledger semantics (acceptance, undo, groups) have been implemented separately in the fake. One shared-fixture precedent exists: `tests/fixtures/newest-sender-summaries.json` is consumed by both `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/newest_sender_tests.rs` and a frontend test.
Do:
- Extend that pattern to acceptance, undo and group semantics. Define scenario files (JSON under `tests/fixtures/`, one per scenario or a small set) as a starting mailbox plus an ordered list of steps (a contract command with its arguments, clock advances, provider outcomes where relevant) and the expected observable result of each step: receipt fields, error codes, and a projection of the snapshot (Inbox membership, activity entries and their statuses, undo availability, group state and per-member outcomes).
- Identifiers that legitimately differ between implementations (operation ids, group ids, timestamps) must be referred to symbolically and compared by role, not by value. Everything else is compared exactly. Time must be driven by each side's fake clock or fake timers, never real waiting.
- Write a Rust runner (integration test in `crates/mail-core/tests/`) and a Vitest runner (under `tests/browser-fake/`) that execute the same files. Make the Rust backend under test a parameter: run every scenario against `GmailCore` with the `mail_core::testing` fake provider, and run the scenarios the fixture backend supports (it is archive-only today) against the fixture `MailCore` as well. The next phase replaces the fixture backend, and scenarios that pass on both today are its parity evidence, so say in the report which scenarios run where.
- Minimum coverage: single archive accepted and confirmed; idempotent replay of the same request id; undo inside the 10-second window (cancel-in-place while queued, compensation after it was claimed); undo rejected after expiry; undo rejected when a newer operation superseded the target; read and star setters where supported; group archive with a mixed accept/reject membership, its idempotent replay, group undo with partial results, and the one-shot rule; the `SELECTION`/group size cap; the typed errors for unsupported or invalid commands. Take the exact rules from the existing Rust tests (`crates/mail-core/tests/undo.rs`, the group tests in the Gmail store) and docs (`docs/ux-04-trustworthy-undo.md`, `docs/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md`), not from the fake.
- The Rust core is the source of truth. Where a scenario shows the fake disagreeing with it, fix the fake in this PR if the fix is small and local, and list every such fix with the scenario that exposed it. If a divergence is large, or the Rust core looks like the wrong side, or the two Rust backends disagree with each other in a way the docs do not explain, do not paper over it: keep the scenario, mark the affected side as a named known divergence in the runner (so it is visible, not silently skipped), and report it.
- Prove the net works: temporarily change a semantic on each side in turn (for example the undo window in the fake, then the supersession rule in the Rust core), show the corresponding runner fails, revert, and put what you did and what failed in the PR description. Do not commit the mutations.
- Document the scenario format and how to add one in docs/development.md, and the contract-parity guarantee in docs/current-architecture.md.
Branch: create maintenance/p4-contract-scenarios from the latest origin/main when you start this ticket (fetch first; if PR A has merged by then, you get the new trait name; if not, avoid depending on the trait's name). Validate with `mise run check:all`, then run the new Rust and Vitest scenario targets five times in a row to show they are deterministic.

FINAL REPORT (your last message)
A table of PRs (number, URL, base, head SHA, CI state), test counts before and after, the scenario list with which backends each runs against, every fake fix and every known divergence, the mutation check results, anything that needs a decision, and anything you did not run. Send a short message as soon as PR A is ready for review so the coordinator can merge it while you continue.

## PRs

| PR | Base | Head SHA | CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#50](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/50) selection | main | 9b9b33c | `check` passed on GitHub |
| [#51](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/51) groups | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-selection` | 2d338c0 | none until retargeted to main |
| [#52](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/52) detail cache | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-groups` | ce3d1cb | none until retargeted to main |
| [#53](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/53) account | `maintenance/p5a-mailbox-detail-cache` | 4adbbc5 | none until retargeted to main |

On each head I ran `mise run test:ui`, typecheck and `build:web`, and all passed. The rendered suite on #53's head is 33 of 34, failing only on the known large-text Inbox row test. I did not run cargo; CI covers the Rust suites. For #51–#53, checks only ran on #50 (the PR targeting main). I never saw them on the stacked PRs.

Every push landed (compared `rev-parse` against `ls-remote`). The pushes for #52 and #53 were rejected once and succeeded on an immediate retry.

## Tests and line counts

- **Test counts:** the baseline I confirmed on main is 1,454 in 84 files. After each PR: #50 1,459 in 85, #51 1,464 in 86, #52 1,473 in 87, #53 1,481 in 88. No test was deleted or weakened.
- **Baseline caveat:** my baseline run overlapped my first edits, but the counts match your 1,454 and everything passed.
- **Line counts:** `useMailbox.ts` is 1,186. The new modules are `useMailboxSelection` 175, `useMailboxGroups` 647, `useMailboxDetailCache` 141, `useMailboxAccount` 177, `mailbox-refs` 10 and `mailbox-session` 20.

## Non-move edits

Each PR description lists these in full:
- **Mechanical substitutions inside moved bodies:** `detached` becomes `session.detached` and `mailboxSessionToken` becomes `session.generation`. `commandToken` becomes `commands.next()`/`commands.current()`, and `++navigationIntentToken` becomes `supersedeNavigation()` in the account module. The remaining reads of parent state became small getter arguments.
- **New plain modules:** `mailbox-refs.ts` holds `sameConversation` and `copyRef`. `mailbox-session.ts` holds the `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) and `CommandFence` types.
- **New functions:** `afterAuthoritativeRefresh()` in groups wraps the four group calls that sat inline in `refresh()`. The detail cache gained two accessors, `currentDetailEpoch()` and `adoptablePrefetch()`, replacing direct reads in `loadDetail`. The account module gained `refreshAccountStatus()`, used at the two `refresh()` call sites.
- **Callback split in the account PR:** the account-change and post-disconnect reset blocks stay in `useMailbox` verbatim as `resetForAccountChange()` and `resetAfterDisconnect()`, and the account module calls them through callbacks.
- **Re-exports:** `useMailbox.ts` re-exports `SELECTION_MAX`, `sameConversation`, `GroupNotice`, `AccountState`, `AccountAction` and the three detail-cache constants.
- **Docs:** `docs/current-architecture.md` is updated in each PR.

## Stale-response proof per piece

- **Selection:** it has no async work, so the fence is explicit clearing. Existing proof is `useMailbox-safety.test.ts` "invalidates accepted saves immediately…". I added `useMailbox-selection.test.ts` "drops selection and anchor when the account identity changes or the account disconnects", plus 4 isolated unit tests.
- **Groups:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox-group-recovery.test.ts` "clears group surfaces on disconnect and rejects late old-session responses", "rejects old restart-notice discovery across a same-account reconnect" and "a stale pre-undo status response never overwrites…".
  - New: `useMailboxGroups.unit.test.ts` moves the session itself.
- **Detail cache:**
  - Existing: `navigation-smooth.test.ts` "drops an in-flight prefetch result after the reader closes".
  - New: "drops an in-flight prefetch… after an account change / disconnect", and `useMailboxDetailCache.unit.test.ts`.
  - Removing the epoch bump makes 5 of these fail.
- **Account:**
  - Existing: `useMailbox.test.ts` "guards stale status responses" and "disconnect clears the list and reader and drops stale in-flight responses".
  - New: `useMailboxAccount.unit.test.ts`.

## Needs a decision

- **Detail-cache fence:** it is its epoch, not the session generation. The owner calls `invalidateDetailCache()` on refresh, mutation start, reader close (which account change and disconnect both call) and dispose. The cache only receives `session.detached`. I did not add a generation check because it would change behaviour, but it is easy to add if you want it strictly generation-based.
- **Account PR:** `useMailbox` still owns the session counters, and the account module reaches them only through the two reset callbacks.
- **Frontend lint:** `mise.toml` has no frontend lint task, only Rust ones, so I ran none.

## Design specificity verdict
- **Design review (A):** authored for this product. The terse voice, the honest Status-Is-Sacred tinting and the careful disconnect flow could not belong to another app. The weak spot is the empty states: one sentence and a link on a blank 968px column, with an empty 272px contact column beside it.

## Overall impression
The fixes landed, and several are better than they needed to be: the cause is in words, Connect is explained, and disconnect is trustworthy. What remains is repetition and the leftover header squeeze. The biggest opportunity is deciding which surface owns each fact, so the header and the empty line stop saying the same thing.

## What's working
1. **Disconnect flow.** The warning names exactly what is removed and kept, focus starts on "Keep account", and Esc returns it to "Disconnect…".
2. **Honest state vocabulary.** Pending, failed and unknown stay distinct, and the tint only echoes words. Contrast is 7.7 to 14.7:1.
3. **Discoverability.** Connect Gmail ranks first in the palette while disconnected, and `g a` is named in the rail title and the chord hint.

This is the coordinating thread for the Email OS maintenance programme ("Review Email OS Architecture and Tests"). The user has asked me to manage this thread and PR #34 as part of that programme, so the goal now is to get #34 merged. I review, gate and merge; you bring it to merge-ready.

WHERE THINGS STAND
- PR #34 head is c191432. Its base is main from 8 November, and it now conflicts with main in 13 files: DESIGN.md, docs/development.md, src/App.vue, src/assets/style.css, src/components/ActionOverlay.vue, src/components/ContactPane.vue, src/lib/action-palette.ts, src/lib/browsing-actions.ts, tests/account.component.test.ts, tests/drafts.component.test.ts, tests/g-chord.component.test.ts, tests/provider-destinations.app.test.ts, tests/stars.component.test.ts.
- What changed on main since your base: the drawer-panels and list-contexts UI work (#31, #32: `useReminders`, `useDrawerRows`, `useDraftPreviews`, drawer rows); the frontend tests were consolidated (shared helpers in `tests/helpers.ts` and `tests/support/`, fake timers, tests grouped into feature folders under `tests/`); a rendered real-Chrome suite; `useMailbox.ts` was split into `useMailboxSelection/Groups/DetailCache/Account` (#50 merged, #51–#53 merging within the hour, same public `Mailbox` interface); Rust-side refactors that do not affect you; and CI (`mise run check:all`) on every PR to main. Read docs/development.md and docs/current-architecture.md on main for the current test layout and commands.

STEP 1: bring the branch up to date
- `git fetch origin` and merge origin/main into `impeccable/account-first-run` (merge, not rebase, so the PR history stays reviewable). Resolve every conflict so that main's behaviour and this PR's design changes both survive. Where the two genuinely disagree (for example main reworked a surface you also changed), keep main's structure and re-apply your change on top, and note it for the report.
- Tests: follow main's conventions. Put this PR's new test files in the matching feature folder, use the shared helpers and fake timers instead of local copies, and do not reintroduce helpers main removed. Every test that exists on main must still be present and pass. If one of your deliberate UI changes requires changing an assertion in a main test, list each such change with the reason. No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement.
- Fetch again before final validation and merge main once more if it moved (the remaining `useMailbox` split PRs will land; they do not touch your files).

STEP 2: validate
- Machine: 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 4 GB free disk, shared with one other thread running cargo. One heavy command at a time, including across subagents. Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target before any mise/cargo command and never hardcode a target dir.
- Run `mise run install:ui`, then `mise run check:all`. Baseline on main after the split lands: frontend 1,481 tests in 88 files, mail-core 327, email-os 14. Report your counts.
- Run the rendered suite once on the final head: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome mise run test:rendered`. Baseline on main is 33 of 34; the one failure is the known large-text Inbox row overflow (`tests/browsing/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts`, "collapses overflowing row actions…"). Do not fix or touch that test in this PR. Any other rendered failure is yours to fix. If your header/tab-floor and contact-pane layout rules can be pinned by a rendered test in that suite, add one or two; that replaces the one-off browser measurements with something repeatable.
- Push, confirm the push landed (`git rev-parse HEAD` vs `git ls-remote origin impeccable/account-first-run`), and check that PR #34 shows as mergeable with CI `check` green. The git remote is a proxy URL, so `gh` needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`.

STEP 3: one closing critique
- Run `/impeccable critique` once on the merged head, the same way as before (rendered at 900, 1030 and 1280px), against the 29.5/40 baseline.
- Exit rule, so this converges: fix every P0 or P1 and every regression it finds. Fix P2 items only if each is small and local, in one pass. Then stop. Do not start another critique-and-fix round. Put the remaining P2/P3 items in the PR description as follow-ups.
- After any fix, re-run step 2's checks on the final head.

BOUNDARIES
- Stay within this PR's existing scope. Do not edit `src/composables/useMailbox*.ts`, `src/composables/mailbox-*.ts` or `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` beyond what a conflict resolution strictly requires (another thread is working on the fake's contract tests). No Rust changes.
- Synthetic fixtures only; no real accounts, credentials or Google network. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os.
- If you hit a product decision, or a conflict where you cannot keep both sides' intent, stop and report it with the evidence rather than choosing silently.

FINAL REPORT (your last message)
Head SHA and CI state; test counts (frontend, core, native, rendered); every conflict resolution that needed judgment; every main test whose assertions you changed and why; the critique score and what you fixed after it; remaining follow-ups; and what is still unverified.

No existing test was deleted or weakened.

**Scenarios.** There are 26 files and 45 scenario-by-profile runs, and each run executes on both the Rust runner and the fake.
- **Both profiles** (Gmail core and fixture, the parity evidence for replacing the fixture backend):
  - **Single actions:** archive confirmed, idempotent replay, unarchive, cancel in place while queued, compensation after confirm (including the 9 s boundary), compensation after claim, expiry at 10 s, superseded, failed not undoable.
  - **Groups:** mixed accept/reject membership, idempotent replay including a reordered replay, partial undo, cancelling queued members, expiry, no eligible member, mutual supersession with singles, the 100-member cap, group member failure.
  - **Typed errors:** the invalid-commands scenario.
- **Gmail only:**
  - archive undo restoring only the originally-INBOX messages
  - read setter and undo
  - star setter and undo
  - star with unknown prior
  - retry
  - read and star groups
- **Fixture only:** the fixture rejecting unsupported commands.

**Fake fixes.** Each was exposed by a scenario:
1. Activity is now listed newest acceptance first. It exposed every multi-operation scenario.
2. The worker is now serial. It exposed `undo-compensates-a-claimed-operation` and `group-undo-partial-results`.
3. Group replay fingerprints the sorted member set. It exposed `group-idempotent-replay`.
4. Blank or over-200-byte request ids are now `invalid_request: requestId`. It exposed `invalid-commands`.

I also added an optional mailbox-seed argument to `createBrowserFakeMailClient`.

**Known divergences.** Each is named, still executed, and must fail:
- **KD-1: Gmail core versus fixture core.**
  - After a definite provider failure, the Gmail worker ends its pass in sync-error backoff, so queued group siblings stay `queued`. The fixture worker and the fake keep draining. The docs do not say which is intended.
  - It also makes every Rust run wait out the 5 s bound.
- **KD-2: fake versus native shell.**
  - In fixture mode the shell answers `setRead` and `setReadGroup` with `invalid_request{mode}`. The fake, a comment in `client.ts` and `groups.test.ts` say `read_only`.
  - I did not change the fake, since an existing test and a doc comment assert the other value.
- **KD-3: fake versus both Rust stores.**
  - Both stores accept an undo attempt on an all-ineligible group and mark every member skipped. The fake rejects it with `not_applicable`, which an existing test asserts.
  - The docs only say such a group "offers no enabled Undo".

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Fake undo window 10 s → 11 s | 28 of 46 Vitest runs failed |
| Fake supersession disabled | 4 Vitest runs failed |

- KD-1: should the Gmail worker keep draining after a failed operation? Settle this before the fixture backend is replaced.
- KD-2: which rejection is intended for fixture `setRead` and `setReadGroup`?
- KD-3: should undo on an all-ineligible group be rejected or accepted?

The `useMailbox` split is fully merged (#50 to #53, ticket 19 done), and the shared contract scenarios (ticket 17, #55) are finished and in my gate now. Main is at `def0950`, which also includes the ADR from #45 (docs only, still marked Proposed).

**Contract scenarios (#55)**
- 26 scenario files run against the Gmail core, the fixture core and the browser fake: 45 runs on each side.
- The thread proved the net works by breaking a rule on each side in turn (undo window, supersession) and watching the matching runner fail.
- The scenarios exposed four places where the browser fake disagreed with the Rust core; all four are fixed in the PR: activity ordering, a serial worker, group replay identity, and request-id validation.

**Three disagreements it found and left visible** (each is a named entry that must keep failing until resolved):
1. **Gmail worker stalls siblings after a failure.** When one operation fails definitively, the Gmail worker ends its pass and backs off, so other queued operations stay queued until the next tick. The fixture worker and the fake keep going. This affects real Gmail use: one failed member of a group archive delays the rest. I have not changed it; say if you want the worker to keep draining.
2. **Fixture `setRead` error type.** The native shell answers `invalid_request`, the fake answers `read_only`. This disappears when fixture mode gains read and star in ticket 14.
3. **Undo on a group with no eligible member.** Both Rust stores accept it and mark every member skipped; the fake rejects it. I'll have the fake aligned to the Rust behaviour during ticket 14.

**Next**
- Merge #55 if the gate passes, then launch the fixture unification thread (ticket 14) on Sonnet 5.5. It will stop and report after stage 3, before anything changes default fixture behaviour.
- The PR #34 thread is working through its merge with main.

# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Proposed

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

## Evidence checkpoints

- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.

## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)

1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.

## Risks and decision gates

A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.

The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.

## Behavior inventory and required policy

References are repository-relative; function names identify the reviewed seam. **Blocker** means an unmodified provider-only substitution cannot preserve the contract. It does not mean the staged implementation is infeasible.

| Surface | Fixture today / GmailCore with synthetic provider | Classification and implementation condition |
|---|---|---|
| Account/status | `src-tauri/src/main.rs::Backend::account_status` returns fixture/Connected/Idle, no mutation grant, 18 cached, complete, no timestamp, limit 0. `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` returns Gmail, observed grant, transient Authenticating/Syncing, timestamps and limit 100. | **Blocker** to drop-in. Internal fixture policy must retain fixture mode/identity/capability presentation; disclose initial loading if asynchronous bootstrap is retained. Do not masquerade as a connected Google account. |
| Credentials | Fixture never opens OAuth or Keychain. GmailCore only calls provider methods; shell constructs GmailProvider/Keychain only in Gmail branch. `gmail/types.rs::GmailReadProvider` does not require a secret type. | **Same** possible. Synthetic provider is constructed directly, with no HTTP client or Secrets. Explicit local-ready startup should replace the misleading credential-presence signal in production. |
| Lifecycle | Fixture rejects connect/disconnect/upgrade/sync commands with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`. Gmail disconnect cancels work and clears account/cache. | **Blocker** without fixture admission policy. Preserve errors and prevent synthetic disconnect from erasing local state. |
| Mailbox gates | Fixture archives/restores, rejects read/star singles/groups with `ReadOnly`; some other unsupported commands use mode errors. GmailCore's Boolean mutation grant admits all three dimensions (`accept_action`, `accept_operation`). | **Blocker**. Per-session archive-only gate is required at core admission, not only hidden controls. Retain existing error variants initially; consistency is a separate contract change. |
| Fake controls | `provider.rs::FakeArchiveProvider::from_env`: paused blocks writes cancellation-aware; reject rejects the next write once; success/default succeeds. | **Different-but-acceptable** implementation: preserve exact environment semantics only in SyntheticProvider writes, leaving reads/bootstrap responsive. Never route the variable to GmailProvider. |
| Seed/restart | `store.rs::migrate_and_seed` transaction seeds `conv-01`…`conv-18` once, including archived `conv-06`/`conv-15`; restarts retain facts/history. Gmail discovery fetches Inbox and does not seed archived rows. | **Blocker** without durable synthetic provider state and initial all-seed cache import. A one-time synthetic bootstrap must preserve actual Inbox facts. Existing `GmailCore::load_search_conversation` / `GmailStore::save_search` can preload the two archived seeds explicitly without pretending they are Inbox mail. Ordinary discovery/history intentionally excludes uncached archived bodies (`history_does_not_import_new_archived_thread_bodies_into_the_bounded_cache`). Reopening an in-memory default provider is insufficient. |
| Undo/clock | `clock.rs`, both stores and both `open_with_clock` facades use 10 seconds and persisted acceptance/preimages; undo may cancel queued work or enqueue compensation. | **Same** core guarantee. Use injected Clock for deadlines; worker Condvar/Instant scheduling still needs bounded waits/notifications. Preserve strict boundary, immutable targets, partial groups, restart and supersession tests. |
| Reminders | `store/reminders.rs::put_reminder` stages archive, worker reconciles removing/pending/returning states and restores prior membership. GmailStore reminders hide locally, do not write provider; no-reply requires connected fresh complete thread read plus account/generation/revision fences (`gmail/sync.rs`, `gmail/store.rs`, UX-11). | **Blocker** to exact parity. Recommended explicit product adjustment: synthetic mode adopts Gmail's local reminder rules, with no Google I/O and fresh reads from the durable synthetic provider. Update fixture disclosures and tests; archive/restore failure-phase tests become obsolete only for that approved adjustment. Do not claim a prototype reminder proves legacy parity. |
| Search | `lib.rs::search_mail` / `store.rs::search_mail` evaluate cached fixture data. Gmail `search_mail` can progressively scan provider candidates with bounded incomplete coverage. | **Same** if fixture policy forces cached-only semantics and all 18 are cached; do not silently enable Gmail discovery/search controls. |
| Saved split | Both facades/store paths validate and persist one account-scoped split; no provider write or undo supersession. | **Same**, provided account stays `fixture-account`; port restart and undo coexistence assertion. |
| Done | Both expose `list_cached_done`, bounded paging, local archive evidence and undo-aware projection. Initially archived rows alone are not necessarily Done evidence. | **Same** guarantee; keep initial seed and pending/restart projection tests. |
| Trash/Starred | Fixture rejects cached Trash (`InvalidRequest`, mode) and Starred (`ReadOnly`), has no star UI; Gmail offers observed bounded caches and star setters. | **Blocker** without fixture gates; default SyntheticProvider star/trash facts must not accidentally expose features. |
| Destinations | Fixture rejects catalog/page commands with mode errors. Gmail uses account-bound trait methods and separate snapshots. | **Same** with policy rejection; no synthetic destination implementation needed for parity. |
| Attachments | Shell fabricates one `fixture-text` descriptor from first message and exact validated text bytes. GmailCore reads persisted descriptors and provider bytes (`list_attachments`, `download_attachment`). | **Different-but-acceptable** ownership: generate the same descriptor/bytes in synthetic data/provider, preserve filename, limits, exact-target revalidation/cancellation and inert Downloads handling. Keep shell transfer security common. |
| Reply context | Fixture reader has safe synthetic reply headers; shell checks complete/latest source; Gmail uses cached context then account-fenced metadata enrichment (`load_reply_context`). | **Same** possible by building complete deterministic synthetic reply metadata, including hostile literal bodies, sender identity and references. No network required. |
| Local drafts | Shared DraftCore in `<selected-profile>/local-drafts`, revision receipts/tombstones and close flush; account derives from selected backend. | **Same** only if profile path and fixture account/mailbox stay stable. Drafts must survive mailbox reset. |
| Pacing/backoff/caps | HTTP provider owns 100ms request spacing (`gmail/provider.rs::pace`); GmailCore owns 60s periodic passes, exponential retry up to 600s, 100 conversation discovery cap, 100 pages/stage, bounded DTO pages. Fixture archive worker has no discovery polling. | **Different-but-acceptable**: SyntheticProvider has no HTTP pacing; 18 fits caps. Seed bootstrap must finish before ready. Fake pause/reject must not stall discovery. Disable needless periodic synthetic discovery or make stable empty history cheap; determinism comes from fixed data, durable facts, injected time and event barriers, not wall-clock sleeps. Explicit requests wake backoff. |

No real store bug was established in this investigation. The mismatches above are existing intentional policy differences or prototype limitations; this spike changes none of them.

## On-disk transition

Today startup selects `<app_data>/fixture-profile/mail.db`; `Store::migrate_and_seed` owns fixture schema versions through 4 and seed version 1. GmailStore opens `gmail.db` with unrelated tables/migrations. Opening that new file beside `mail.db` is not a migration. `docs/development.md` promises seeds never reset provider facts or operation history; `docs/current-status.md` promises durable synthetic state and drafts. A silent reset violates that promise.

Choose **reset with disclosure and retained backup**, not an operation-ledger migration, for the eventual implementation. Before changing fixture storage, show a one-time explicit disclosure that synthetic mailbox actions, history, reminders and saved split start fresh; do not automatically approve or execute it as part of this ADR. Keep old `mail.db` and its journal/WAL state safely backed up under the profile lease using a consistent SQLite backup, not a live raw file copy. Record the transition atomically so crashes cannot repeatedly reset the new profile. Never apply this transition to `gmail-profile` or credentials. The implementation must cover cancel, crash/restart, insufficient disk and backup failure before switching.

Retain `<fixture-profile>/local-drafts` untouched, along with its account identity and fixture mailbox, so draft references to fixed conversation/message IDs remain meaningful. Do not recursively delete the fixture directory. Test opening old drafts and reply source references after the new seed bootstrap. Update development/status/fixture documentation to state the one-time reset; thereafter retain seed-once/restart persistence. A migration preserving pending preimages/groups/reminder revisions would cost more and needs its own mapping; this proposal deliberately does not promise it.

## Wire and frontend contract

No DTO shape, generated TypeScript definition, IPC command name or event name needs to change. `dto.rs`, `gmail/types.rs`, `groups.rs`, `reminders.rs`, `src/lib/ipc/client.ts`, `tauri-client.ts` and `generated.ts` can remain the wire source of truth. This spike changes none. A naive switch would change **values and errors** visible on that wire: mode, grant, connection/sync state, coverage count, unsupported command errors and reminder phases. The staged policy must preserve the former values/errors, with the explicitly disclosed local-reminder and initial-loading adjustment above; run generated-contract checks even if no DTO edit is expected.

`src/composables/useMailbox.ts` uses mode and mutation access for Gmail upgrade/action controls. `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts` and browser fake controls model Gmail stars/destinations separately. `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` defaults to fixture, seeds in-memory synthetic conversations, implements simulated-Gmail mode/grants, uses `fixture-text` attachments, fake reply metadata and in-memory operation/reminder ledgers. `fixture-workspaces.ts` also permits overlapping IDs across two isolated synthetic accounts. It remains a browser implementation, not a production provider dependency. Frontend/browser tests establish capability gating, identities, error/receipt rendering, deterministic selection and fake timers; they do not establish SQLite durability, OAuth or native provider behavior. Preserve their fixture/default assumptions and add boundary tests for synthetic native status; do not r

## Size, risk and fallback

Measured source sizes at baseline: fixture `store.rs` 4,030 lines (2,647 before unit tests), `worker.rs` 200, `seed.rs` 327, `provider.rs` 211, fixture `store/reminders.rs` 341; reminder unit/race files 377 combined. Those five principal files total **5,109 lines**, including embedded tests/data; seed data and cancellation infrastructure must move rather than vanish. `lib.rs` is 630 lines (facade/test portions removable, public shared modules remain); the shell Backend implementation occupies about 380 lines plus subscription variants. Including removable facade/shell forwarding, roughly **4,000–4,500 non-test lines removed or replaced**, and roughly **5,000–6,000 gross lines** including relocated tests/data; do not present gross deletion as net savings.

Planning estimate, not a prototype diff: add/retain 500–900 lines of production synthetic data/provider persistence, 150–350 lines of session policy/bootstrap and 150–300 lines of transition/disclosure logic, plus 500–1,200 lines of ports/contract tests. Reminder policy work may exceed this. Net production reduction is plausibly 1,000–2,000 lines, contingent on review. Removing 23 duplicated group/undo helpers (~730 lines) is a concrete payoff, not proof the whole rewrite is cheap. Main risks are synthetic facts being overwritten on restart; archived seeds omitted; grants accidentally broadened; reminder semantic drift; draft loss from broad reset; crash-safe backup; shared-core regressions in Gmail; and a long migration with two enabled paths. Each stage must retain working defaults and pass targeted core, contract and native bridge checks; final UI/end-to-end gates belong to 

If the policy/bootstrap/reminder cost becomes unacceptable, **no-go fallback**: keep both stores and extract only the duplicated ledger algorithms. Define a private `OperationLedgerStorage` seam over an already-owned transaction: load operation/preimage/group rows, enumerate ordered members and newer intent, persist undo decisions/links/receipts, and insert compensation. Shared typed structs carry operation status/dimension/targets, while each adapter owns SQL/table/column names (`operations` vs `gmail_operations`, `failure_kind` vs `last_error`) and row conversion. Pass Clock/now explicitly. Transaction ownership, admission, provider execution, reconciliation and reminder semantics stay in each store; avoid a generic SQL string interpolation framework. Port both existing test matrices before removing helpers. Estimate 250–450 lines of adapters and 100–200 of shared types/glue replac

## Relationship to PR #44

Read `origin/maintenance/p1-rust-test-foundations` at `3814d95` (PR [#44](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/44)), including `testing.rs` and `testing/operations_fake.rs`. Its `test-support` module provides bounded waits/temp profiles/DTO builders and scripted provider outcomes/hooks for cancellation, uncertain dispatch and account races. Use it for ports once merged; rebase in coordinator order. A production SyntheticProvider **must not enable or import test-support** and must not carry its mutable scripts/hooks. Share `GmailReadProvider`, production DTOs and any genuinely pure production data conversion functions in the dependency direction **testing → production**. Fixed fixture data should move from `seed.rs` into a production synthetic module; scripted fakes remain test-only and can wrap the synthetic provider when useful. Do not turn the built-in offline fixture into an 


## Prototype evidence and limits

The separate [throwaway prototype branch](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype) contains only additive test code, based on `58e0bc7`; it is **not for merge**. It constructs `SyntheticProvider` directly and runs real GmailCore/GmailStore SQL, using the repository's actual seed via a test-local path import. There is no Google HTTP client, credentials store, OAuth or Keychain construction. `has_credentials() = true` is a readiness shim that selects startup restore; it does not represent a token. `mutation_access() = true` enables the experiment's archive operations and demonstrates why production needs the separate archive-only policy.

Ordinary discovery gives the correct 16-row Inbox. The harness explicitly preloads the two archived seed conversations through `load_search_conversation`; cached search then lists all 18 and the reader checks every fixed ID/subject/message count with the original Inbox facts. The remaining flows use a frozen injected clock: confirmed single archive then compensating Undo; confirmed two-member archive group then group Undo; shutdown and reopen with a **new provider object** reading its saved facts; replay of the same durable SQLite acceptance receipt; and a future local reminder that hides locally then returns after clock advancement. The timer experiment follows Gmail reminder rules, not fixture archive/restore phases.

Special cases still required before production: move seed data into a normal production module; make provider facts transactional/crash-durable (the prototype uses non-atomic JSON and defaults missing/malformed JSON to seed facts); model archive per message rather than per conversation; replace readiness/grant shims with explicit fixture policy; replace full-catalog history replay with stable synthetic change tracking; preserve fake pause/reject cancellation semantics; populate synthetic attachments/reply metadata; implement profile transition and port the remaining guarantees below. No test-support feature is enabled or imported. This is evidence that the existing ledger can serve synthetic mail, not evidence of full fixture parity or Gmail/platform correctness.

Validated prototype head [`0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37`](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/commit/0d6c482daee125c8246daf822db46067fbea6b37): `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target cargo test -p mail-core --test synthetic_provider_spike` — **1 passed, 0 failed**. The one integration test runs every flow above; it is not the full regression suite. Only warning: the path-imported seed module has an unused `SEED_VERSION`. Targeted Rust work was serialized after checking the sibling build slot; no frontend suite or broad Rust build was run for this spike. Production sources, DTOs and lockfile remain unchanged. `git diff --check` passed for the ADR.

input.title: P4b: fixture on the Gmail core (ticket 14, stages 1–3)
input.message:
You are implementing ticket 14 of the Email OS maintenance programme: run fixture mode on the Gmail core with a built-in synthetic provider, so the operation ledger (acceptance, undo, groups, reminders) exists once in Rust instead of twice. You do stages 1 to 3 of ADR 0002 in this thread. Stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the old backend) is NOT yours: you stop after stage 3 and report.

I am the coordinating thread. I gate and merge your PRs; you never merge. You can message me at any time with a question, and you should message me when each stage's PR is ready so I can gate it while you continue.

## Read first

- `docs/adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md` — the whole thing. Its behaviour inventory table and its appendix (the test disposition, test by test) are your specification.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/current-status.md`, `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` if present.
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/` — `sync.rs` (GmailCore, `open_with_clock`, the worker), `types.rs` (trait `GmailProvider`; the live implementation is `LiveGmailProvider` in `provider.rs`), `store.rs` and `store/` (18 modules), `store_schema.rs` (ordered migrations, currently `gmail-migrations-9`).
- The fixture side you are replacing later: `crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs` (`MailCore`), `store.rs`, `worker.rs`, `seed.rs`, `provider.rs`, `store/reminders.rs`; and `src-tauri/src/main.rs` (`Backend` enum).
- `crates/mail-core/src/testing.rs` and `testing/` (the `test-support` feature: temp profiles, bounded waits, scripted provider).
- The contract scenarios merged today: `tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios/`, `crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs` (profiles `gmail` and `fixture`, `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`), `tests/browser-fake/contract-scenarios.test.ts`, `tests/support/contract-scenarios.ts`, and the doc that describes the format.
- The prototype branch `origin/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype` is evidence only. Do not merge or copy it wholesale; the ADR lists what it got wrong (non-atomic JSON facts, per-conversation archive, readiness shims).

## Decisions already made

The ADR is merged with Status "Proposed". The project owner asked for the remaining tickets to run, and I am proceeding on these decisions. In your first PR, record them in the ADR under a short "Decisions" section and change the status to "Accepted (stages 1–3)". Word it accurately: these were taken on the coordinator's recommendation, and the owner can still redirect before stage 4.

1. Go with staged unification, as the ADR recommends.
2. Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the ADR's "archive-only" wording, which was about preserving today's errors; the decision is that the unified fixture gains read and star. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules (hide locally, no provider write). The fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. The on-disk transition (stage 4) will be a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup, local drafts untouched. You do not implement it; you plan it.

Everything else in the ADR's table stands: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present including the two initially archived ones (`conv-06`, `conv-15`), the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Hard rules

- **Default behaviour does not change in stages 1 to 3.** With no opt-in set, fixture mode still runs `MailCore` on `fixture-profile/mail.db`, byte for byte as today. Existing fixture tests stay and stay green. Nothing is deleted from the old backend in this thread.
- **Gmail behaviour does not change at all.** The session policy must be a no-op for Gmail. Existing Gmail tests are not edited to make them pass (adding tests is fine; a mechanical signature change is fine if you list every one). Prefer no change to the Gmail database schema. If you truly need one, it is an ordered migration step 10 with a legacy fixture and updated `current-schema.sql`, following `store_schema.rs` and `migration_tests.rs`, and you tell me before you build on it.
- The synthetic provider is production code. It must not enable or import the `test-support` feature. The dependency direction is testing → production. Move the 18-conversation data into a production synthetic module in a way that the old `seed.rs` path keeps working unchanged (share the data, do not fork it).
- Synthetic provider facts must be durable and crash-safe (transactional, not a JSON file rewritten in place), must model archive per message as Gmail does, and must be seeded once: reopening must never overwrite facts that changed. Its storage lives under the fixture profile, in a new file. It never touches `mail.db`, the `gmail-profile`, credentials, or `local-drafts`.
- No DTO shape, generated TypeScript, IPC command name or event name changes. Run `mise run check:contract`.
- Privacy: nothing that logs may include subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids, or SQL with bound values. Storage errors go through `storage_log.rs` as they do today.
- Synthetic data only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network, in code or tests. Tests use injected clocks and event barriers, not wall-clock sleeps.
- Do not touch these frontend files; another PR (#34) that changes them merges within the hour: `src/App.vue`, `src/components/`, `src/assets/style.css`, `src/lib/account-status.ts`, `src/lib/action-palette.ts`, `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts`, `src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue`, `tests/account*`, `tests/layout/`. The only frontend files you should need are `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` and the contract scenario tests. If you believe you need another, ask me first.
- Do not change the Gmail worker's behaviour after a definite failure (known divergence KD-1 in `contract_scenarios.rs`). That is waiting on the owner.

## The three stages, one PR each

Stack the branches (`maintenance/p4-synthetic-stage1`, `-stage2`, `-stage3`). The stage 1 PR targets `main`; the others target the branch below. CI only runs on PRs whose base is `main`, so each stage must pass `mise run check:all` locally before you mark its PR ready. Open each PR as a draft and mark it ready when green. Message me when each one is ready.

**Stage 1 — port the guarantees, add the provider.**
- Record the decisions in the ADR (above).
- Production synthetic data module and `SyntheticGmailProvider` implementing `GmailProvider`, constructed directly, with durable facts.
- Port the fixture guarantees to tests that run against `GmailCore` + the synthetic provider, following the ADR appendix test by test. Keep a table in the PR description: each appendix entry → the new test, or "obsolete under decision N", or "deferred to stage 2/3 because …". Nothing silently dropped.
- Fix known divergence KD-3 on the fake's side: undo on a group whose members are all ineligible is accepted by both Rust stores with members marked skipped, and rejected by the browser fake with `not_applicable`. Align the fake to Rust, remove the `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entry (the runner tells you if an entry no longer fails), and keep that in its own commit.

**Stage 2 — explicit session policy and seeding.**
- An explicit internal session policy in `GmailCore` (not a scattering of `if fixture` checks): identity and status (`fixture` mode, `fixture-account`, connected/idle presentation per the ADR table, no mutation "grant" masquerading as a Google permission), admission (decision 2), lifecycle rejections, cached-only search, local readiness in place of the `has_credentials()` restore signal, and non-destructive lifecycle. Gmail's policy is the existing behaviour, unchanged.
- Seed-once bootstrap that finishes before the session reports ready, including the two initially archived conversations, without pretending they are Inbox mail. Initially archived rows are not Done evidence.
- No needless periodic synthetic discovery, or make a stable empty history cheap. Fake pause/reject must not stall reads or bootstrap.
- Add a `synthetic` profile to the Rust contract scenario runner and run every scenario on it. It should match the `gmail` profile except where the policy says otherwise; any difference is either a named, justified entry or a bug you fix. KD-2 (fixture `setRead` errors) concerns the old `fixture` profile and stays listed until stage 4; note in the PR what the fake will need at stage 4.

**Stage 3 — reminders, attachments, reply metadata, opt-in launch.**
- Reminders on the synthetic session under the Gmail local rules, with acceptance, race and restart tests (injected clock). Fresh reads come from the durable synthetic provider.
- The synthetic `fixture-text` attachment (same descriptor, filename, exact bytes, limits, exact-target revalidation, cancellation) and deterministic reply metadata (including the hostile literal bodies, sender identity and references) served through the provider/core seams rather than fabricated in the shell. The shell's transfer security stays common. The old shell path keeps working for the default backend.
- An opt-in launch path: an environment variable (suggest `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE=1`, fixture mode only, ignored in Gmail mode) that makes the shell run fixture mode on `GmailCore` + the synthetic provider with its own database file under the fixture profile. `local-drafts` is shared and untouched, `mail.db` is never opened for writing on this path. Document it in `docs/development.md` as a validation path, not a user feature. I will run my native smoke test on it, so the 18 conversations, archive, undo, reader, search, drafts and reminders must work end to end through the real Tauri commands. Add native bridge tests in `src-tauri` for it.

## Then stop and report

Do not start stage 4. Your final report must include:
- The three PRs with head SHAs, and for each: test counts for `mail-core`, `email-os` and the frontend (baseline on main today: 328, 14, and 1,527 in 89 files), and confirmation `check:all` passed.
- The appendix disposition table, complete.
- Every existing test you edited, with the reason.
- A stage 4 plan: the switch, the disclosure and backup-reset design (cancel, crash/restart, insufficient disk, backup failure), exactly what gets deleted, and what the browser fake and docs need.
- A UI impact inventory for stage 4: every user-visible difference between today's fixture mode and the synthetic one (status values, loading states, read/star controls appearing, reminder phases, error text, anything else you found), each with where in the frontend it surfaces.
- What you could not verify.

## Working on this machine

- 2 cores, 7 GB RAM, about 6 GB of free disk, shared with one other agent thread and my gate runs. Run one cargo build or test at a time, never two in parallel, and no more than two subagents at once. Use `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target` (the shared target directory) for every cargo and mise invocation; do not create another target directory. If free disk drops under 2 GB, stop and message me.
- Do not modify the working tree of the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` (it has an uncommitted change that belongs to the owner). Work only in your worktree.
- Run `pnpm install` in your worktree before frontend checks. Tasks are in `mise.toml`: `test:core`, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `check:contract`, `lint:core`, `lint:native`, `typecheck`, `build:web`, `check:all`.
- Use subagents for self-contained pieces (for example, porting one appendix section of tests, or an independent review of the session policy diff before you mark stage 2 ready). Subagents run on the same model as you. Give them the hard rules above.
- After each push, confirm the remote head matches your local head (`git ls-remote`). `gh` commands need `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`.
